llm.summary: The skill's content aligns with a Kubernetes/Openshift multi-agent operator, but the runtime instructions require broad cluster/cloud/registry access that the registry metadata does not declare — this mismatch and the wide-ranging command-level instructions warrant caution before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill name and description (Kubernetes / OpenShift multi-agent swarm) match the provided SKILL.md and per-agent documentation: abilities described (kubectl/oc operations, GitOps, registry management, CVE scanning) are coherent with its stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instruction files contain explicit commands that read and modify cluster state (kubectl/oc), manage cloud resources (aws/az/gcloud/rosa/aro), and interact with registries (jfrog, Harbor, ACR, ECR). The docs include examples that create secrets, rotate credentials, run image promotion, and call external registry APIs — all of which require sensitive credentials and can alter infrastructure. Although the skill claims 'human-in-the-loop' guardrails, many imperative command examples are present and could be executed by an agent with access.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is instruction-only with no install spec or executable downloads, which reduces filesystem/remote-code risk. Risk depends on the host CLIs that run (kubectl, cloud CLIs, trivy, jfrog, etc.) rather than code pulled by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The registry metadata lists no required env vars/credentials, yet the SKILL.md repeatedly assumes KUBECONFIG and access to cloud provider credentials and registry credentials (examples reference ARTIFACTORY_USER/TOKEN, HARBOR_USER/PASSWORD, AWS/az/gcloud auth). This mismatch is concerning: the skill effectively requires high-privilege credentials but does not declare or scope them, increasing the chance of misconfiguration or secret exposure.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no install script are good, but the skill expects to append to local log files (logs/LOGS.md, memory/MEMORY.md, incidents/INCIDENTS.md) and perform potentially privileged cluster operations. Autonomous model invocation is allowed (model_invocation: true); combined with the broad operational capabilities and un-declared credential needs, that expands the blast radius if the agent is granted cluster/cloud access without strict controls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to be a comprehensive, instruction-only Kubernetes agent swarm — which is coherent with its description — but it assumes access to cluster credentials (KUBECONFIG), cloud provider CLIs and registry credentials that the registry metadata does not declare. Before installing or enabling this skill: 1) Treat it as requiring real cluster and registry credentials — only run it against a test cluster first. 2) Use least-privilege service accounts (no cluster-admin for routine operations) and narrow IAM policies for cloud/registry access. 3) Require and verify human-approval gating for any destructive or production-change commands. 4) Ensure logs and memory files (logs/LOGS.md, memory/MEMORY.md, INCIDENTS.md) are written to a controlled location with proper access controls and retention. 5) Consider disabling autonomous invocation or restricting the agent's role-binding while you audit the SKILL.md agent instructions in detail. 6) If you need to proceed, explicitly map which environment variables and credentials will be provided and why (KUBECONFIG, ARTIFACTORY_*, HARBOR_*, AWS/AZ/GCLOUD auth), and prefer ephemeral, scoped credentials and out-of-band human approval for high-risk operations.
